extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (primary) and patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidance for applying 35 U.S.C. §101 at examination, implementing the USPTO's 2019 Revised Patent Subject Matter Eligibility Guidance (2019 PEG). Covers the revised two-prong Step 2A, Step 2B inventive-concept analysis, abstract-idea groupings, and related examiner procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revised Step 2A two-prong inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Under revised Step 2A, a claim is eligible at Step 2A unless it (1) recites a judicial exception and (2) the exception is not integrated into a practical application of the exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prong One: determine whether the claim recites a judicial exception (abstract idea, law of nature, or natural phenomenon). If no exception is recited, the claim is eligible and analysis ends. If an exception is recited, go to Prong Two. Prong Two: determine whether additional elements integrate the exception into a practical application; if so the claim is eligible, otherwise the claim is "directed to" the exception and proceed to Step 2B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prong One — recitation of judicial exceptions (laws/natural phenomena)
rubrics_metrics.description: For laws of nature and natural phenomena, continue to use the 'recite' standard set forth in MPEP 2106.04(b) and (c), including markedely different characteristics analysis, to determine if a claim recites a law of nature or natural phenomenon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the claim recites a law of nature or natural phenomenon (including a product of nature), proceed to Prong Two.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prong One — recitation of abstract ideas (use groupings)
rubrics_metrics.description: For abstract ideas, Prong One requires identifying the specific limitation(s) that the examiner believes recite an abstract idea, and determining whether those limitation(s) fall within at least one of the groupings of abstract ideas enumerated in the 2019 PEG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use the prior "Eligibility Quick Reference Sheet Identifying Abstract Ideas." Claim limitations that do not fall within the enumerated groupings should not be treated as abstract ideas except in rare circumstances (see procedure for tentative abstract ideas). If a limitation falls within any grouping, proceed to Prong Two.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping: Mathematical concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract ideas that are mathematical concepts, including mathematical relationships, mathematical formulas or equations, and mathematical calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limitations that amount to mathematical relationships/formulas/calculations should be considered under this grouping when determining if a claim recites an abstract idea at Prong One.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping: Mental processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract ideas that are concepts performed in the human mind, including observation, evaluation, judgment, or opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims reciting activities that can be performed in the human mind fall within this grouping; note that recitation of generic computer components does not necessarily preclude recitation of an abstract idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping: Certain methods of organizing human activity
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract ideas involving methods of organizing human activity, including fundamental economic principles or practices (hedging, insurance, mitigating risk), commercial or legal interactions (contracts, legal obligations, advertising, marketing, sales), and managing personal behavior or relationships or interactions between people (social activities, teaching, following rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this grouping for business-commercial-legal and interpersonal organizational concepts when evaluating Prong One.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prong Two — integration into a practical application (general standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Integration into a practical application" requires an additional element or combination of additional elements in the claim to apply, rely on, or use the judicial exception in a manner that imposes a meaningful limit on the judicial exception, such that the claim is more than a drafting effort designed to monopolize the exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate additional elements using considerations from Supreme Court and Federal Circuit decisions and MPEP 2106.05 subsections; most Prong Two considerations mirror those used in Step 2B, but do not include WURC analysis. If the exception is integrated into a practical application under these considerations, the claim is eligible at Prong Two.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prong Two considerations — limitations indicative of integration into a practical application
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain types of additional claim limitations are indicative that the judicial exception is integrated into a practical application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicative limitations include: improvements to functioning of a computer or other technology/technical field (MPEP 2106.05(a)); applying/using an exception to effect a particular treatment or prophylaxis for a disease/medical condition (per Vanda memo); applying/using the exception with/by a particular machine (MPEP 2106.05(b)); effecting a transformation or reduction of a particular article to a different state or thing (MPEP 2106.05(c)); applying/using the exception in some other meaningful way beyond generally linking it to a technological environment or field of use (MPEP 2106.05(e) and Vanda memo).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prong Two considerations — limitations not indicative of integration into a practical application
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain claim recitations are not indicative that a judicial exception has been integrated into a practical application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not indicative: merely adding the words 'apply it' (or equivalent), mere instructions to implement an abstract idea on a computer, or merely using a computer as a tool to perform an abstract idea (MPEP 2106.05(f)); adding insignificant extra-solution activity (MPEP 2106.05(g)); generally linking use of the judicial exception to a particular technological environment or field of use (MPEP 2106.05(h)). Note: whether elements are well-understood, routine, conventional (WURC) is NOT evaluated at Prong Two.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not evaluate WURC at Prong Two (WURC exclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether claim elements represent only well-understood, routine, conventional activity (WURC) is considered at Step 2B and is NOT a consideration at Step 2A Prong Two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should give weight to all claimed additional elements in Prong Two, even if those elements represent WURC activity. Do not assess WURC unless the analysis proceeds to Step 2B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2B — inventive concept (aka 'significantly more')
rubrics_metrics.description: At Step 2B, evaluate whether the claim recites additional elements that amount to an inventive concept — i.e., whether the claim as a whole amounts to 'significantly more' than the recited judicial exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: identify additional elements beyond the judicial exception, evaluate those elements individually and in combination to determine if they amount to significantly more, using considerations in MPEP 2106.05 and relevant case law. If inventive concept present, claim is eligible; if not, claim is ineligible. Step 2B uses WURC analysis (unlike Prong Two).

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2B considerations — limitations indicative of an inventive concept
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations that tend to indicate presence of an inventive concept overlap with Prong Two indicative limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicative of inventive concept: improvements to functioning of a computer or other technology (MPEP 2106.05(a)); applying the judicial exception with/by a particular machine (b); effecting a transformation of an article (c); applying/using the judicial exception in some other meaningful way beyond linking it to a technological environment (e); adding a specific limitation other than what is well-understood, routine, conventional activity in the field (d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2B considerations — limitations not indicative of an inventive concept
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations that do not indicate an inventive concept at Step 2B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not indicative: merely adding 'apply it' or equivalent or mere instructions to implement on a computer (MPEP 2106.05(f)); adding insignificant extra-solution activity (MPEP 2106.05(g)); generally linking to a technological environment or field of use (MPEP 2106.05(h)); simply appending well-understood, routine, conventional activities specified at a high level of generality (MPEP 2106.05(d) and Berkheimer memo). Note that WURC is evaluated at Step 2B and may defeat an inventive-concept finding unless elements are unconventional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for tentative abstract ideas (non-enumerated)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner believes a claim limitation should be treated as an abstract idea even though it does not fall within the enumerated groupings, the limitation may be treated as a 'tentative abstract idea' in rare circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the claim under the 2019 PEG: if the claim as a whole integrates the tentative abstract idea into a practical application, the claim is eligible; otherwise proceed to Step 2B. In Step 2B, if the claim provides an inventive concept, the claim is eligible; otherwise the examiner must bring the application to the TC director. Any rejection based on a tentative abstract idea requires TC director approval (to be indicated in the file record) and must justify why the limitation is being treated as reciting an abstract idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners' procedure when applicants argue eligibility (applications in process)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant argues that previously rejected claims are eligible, examiners should re-evaluate each claim under the 2019 PEG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a claim is now eligible, withdraw the 35 U.S.C. 101 rejection. If the claim remains ineligible, update the form paragraph(s) used and ensure the rejection explanation addresses why the claim recites a judicial exception, fails to integrate the exception into a practical application, and fails to provide an inventive concept. Examiners should also consider other patentability statutes (35 U.S.C. 102, 103, 112) and consult the FAQ for guidance on final rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph and documentation requirements for 101 rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of updated form paragraphs and documentation practices for 35 U.S.C. 101 rejections under the 2019 PEG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.05.016 is the new paragraph for 'Directed to a judicial exception without an inventive concept/significantly more' for enumerated abstract ideas, laws of nature, or natural phenomena. Form paragraph 7.05.017 must be used (with TC director approval) for abstract ideas that are not enumerated in the 2019 PEG. Examiners must update form paragraph cross-references and provide explanations in the file that address recitation, lack of integration into a practical application, and lack of inventive concept. Prior paragraph 7.05.015 is superseded/deleted.

rubrics_metrics.name: General reminders and prosecutorial practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Key takeaways about claim-level analysis and prosecution practice under the 2019 PEG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the claim as a whole and consider all recited limitations when determining eligibility. Do not use the old Eligibility Quick Reference Sheet for abstract idea identification. WURC is considered at Step 2B, not Step 2A. The key inquiry in revised Step 2A is whether a claim that recites a judicial exception is directed to the judicial exception itself or to a practical application of the judicial exception. Practice compact prosecution: address all statutory requirements (not just eligibility) and point applicants to eligible subject matter in the specification when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of examples and supporting resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO provides examples and resources to demonstrate application of the 2019 PEG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New examples (37-42) analyze hypothetical claims under the 2019 PEG (including abstract ideas, computer-related inventions, and software). Examples 1-36 were issued prior to the 2019 PEG and may not be entirely consistent with it; claims previously indicated eligible remain eligible but use those earlier examples with caution. Additional resources: MPEP 2106 (except superseded portions), Berkheimer memo, subject matter eligibility webpage, sample rejections, and FAQ document.
